rationale: C09 is the strongest candidate because it states the administration's specific proposed mechanism for sugar quotas shortly before the child: presidential authority to reduce a foreign country's quota when the President determines that action to be in the national interest. The child implements materially the same mechanism after congressional enactment, applying it to Cuba and repeating the national-interest determination. Although C09 is a letter rather than a proclamation and does not supply the child's full operative structure, its specialized sugar-quota language plausibly supplied a concrete part of the later drafting. C19 and C15 offer closer proclamation form and commodity-quota machinery, but their shared features are more generic and arise under different statutes.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the President shall determine... the quota for Cuba... in such amount or amounts as he shall find from time to time to be in the national interest
shared_material.parent_excerpt: give me the authority to reduce the quota for a calendar year for any foreign country... when I determine it to be in the national interest
shared_material.explanation: Both describe the same specialized presidential mechanism: reducing a foreign country's sugar quota upon a national-interest determination.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Do hereby determine that in the national interest the quota for Cuba... for the balance of calendar year 1960 shall be 39,752 short tons
shared_material.parent_excerpt: authority to reduce the quota for a calendar year for any foreign country... when I determine it to be in the national interest
shared_material.explanation: The child's operative determination concretely exercises the authority anticipated in C09, adapting the general proposal to Cuba and a specified quota amount.
